---
title: "Get Started"
subtitle: "Download Emaki, install an agent, and open a project."
---

{{< include _sk/index.html >}}

::: {.steps}

1.  ### Download Emaki

    ::: {.downloads}
    <a class="download" data-os="mac" data-chip="arm64" href="https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest/download/Emaki-mac-arm64.dmg"><strong>macOS</strong> <span>Apple silicon</span></a>
    <a class="download" data-os="mac" data-chip="x64" href="https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest/download/Emaki-mac-x64.dmg"><strong>macOS</strong> <span>Intel</span></a>
    <a class="download" data-os="windows" href="https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest/download/Emaki-windows-x64-setup.exe"><strong>Windows</strong> <span>x64 installer</span></a>
    <a class="download" data-os="linux" href="https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest/download/Emaki-linux-x64.AppImage"><strong>Linux</strong> <span>x64 AppImage</span></a>
    :::

    The Mac image is signed and notarized and needs macOS 14 or later.
    Windows is unsigned, so SmartScreen asks once: *More info*, then *Run
    anyway*. On Linux run the AppImage, or install the `.deb` from the
    [release page](https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest).
    From then on the app updates itself.

2.  ### Install an agent

    Emaki works with Claude Code and Codex. Install one or both, and sign in.

    ::: {.agents}

    ::: {.agent .agent-claude}
    **Claude Code**

    [Install it](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code), then run
    `claude` once to sign in.
    :::

    ::: {.agent .agent-codex}
    **Codex**

    [Install it](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli), then run `codex`
    once to sign in.
    :::

    :::

    Not sure what this machine has? The Agents page ([⌘E]{.kbd}) checks,
    and walks you through installing one, a step at a time, with a shell
    beside the steps.

3.  ### GitHub, if you want it

    Git is optional. With it, Emaki shows a project's changes and branches
    and commits for you; signed in to GitHub, it fetches, pulls and pushes
    too. The Agents page has the steps: install git, sign in with `gh`,
    and tell git who your commits are by.

:::

## Open a project {.i-folder}

Pick a folder, choose the agent, and type. That is a session, in that
folder, and its tab and its row in the sidebar appear at once. Or pick up
one the agent already has: every session on the machine is listed under
its project, from both agents. The first launch copies every Claude Code
transcript into `~/.emaki/archive`, and each later launch catches up, so
a session the agent has deleted is still here. See
[Projects](projects.qmd).

## The window {.i-app-window}

The chat is the main panel. Four panels stand beside it, a button
and a key each, there when you want them and gone when you do not.

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| [Files](files.qmd) | [⌘⇧F]{.kbd} | the project's folder as a tree, a pane for any file, and git |
| [Outline](outline.qmd) | [⌘⇧O]{.kbd} | a label for every prompt, to jump back to any step |
| [Shell Terminal](shell.qmd) | [⌘⇧S]{.kbd} | a shell in the project's folder |
| [Agent Terminal](agent.qmd) | [⌘⇧A]{.kbd} | the session's own agent as it runs |

: {.table-keys tbl-colwidths="[30,14,56]"}

Files and outline share the left side, one at a time; the two terminals
share the right.

## What it keeps {.i-hard-drive}

Everything is under `~/.emaki`:

| | |
|---|---|
| `archive/` | every Claude Code session, copied byte for byte |
| `logs/` | each session rendered as markdown |
| `search.db` | the full-text index |
| `config.json` | your settings |

: {.table-keys tbl-colwidths="[24,76]"}

Only `archive/` cannot be rebuilt. That is the folder to back up.

Emaki sets one thing in Claude Code's settings: its status line, which
feeds the [status bar](chats.qmd#the-status-bar) under the
composer. `emaki-core statusline restore` puts yours back.
